Below is a framework you can adapt to your market’s local laws and to Airbnb’s own rules (Airbnb forbids any recording in “private spaces” without explicit, prior guest consent). The goal is to preserve real security value—deterring break-ins, documenting emergencies or liability events—while fully respecting your guests’ right to privacy.

1. Know the Rules First  
 • Airbnb policy: No cameras or audio recorders in bedrooms, bathrooms, or any space where guests expect privacy. You must disclose all recording devices in your listing before guests book.  
 • Local law: Many jurisdictions require “one-party” or “two-party” consent for audio recording. Even if video-only, check statutes on “expectation of privacy.”  
 • GDPR/CCPA (if applicable): If you host EU or California residents, treat recordings as “personal data,” provide a brief privacy notice, allow access/deletion requests.

2. Choose the Right Equipment  
 • Video-only (no audio) is simplest from a legal standpoint. If you must have audio, explicitly disclose and secure guest opt-in.  
 • Motion-activated vs. continuous: Motion triggers cut down stored footage and focus on events.  
 • Local storage vs. cloud: Encrypted cloud storage can guard against camera tampering; local DVR/NVR keeps you fully in control (remember to encrypt disks).  
 • Camera form-factor:  
   – Flush-mount domes or small bullet cams painted to match eaves/fascia for discreetness  
   – Lens angle 100°–120° for wide coverage without excessive zoom  
   – IR night vision for exterior lighting conditions

3. Ideal Placement Zones  
(Always outside “private” guest areas. Mark them clearly on your house rules map.)

  A. Outdoor Perimeter  
   • Over front door or porch—captures package deliveries, forced-entry attempts  
   • Back door/patio gate—checks on unauthorized late-night access  
   • Driveway/garage—vehicle arrivals/departures; preferred to mount 10–12ft high, angled down  

  B. Common Indoor Areas (if you rent an entire home and have a true shared-use space)  
   • Entry foyer or vestibule—good “choke point” to see who walks in  
   • Hallway junction (if your layout leads guest traffic past a corner)  
   • Kitchen or living room corner—not pointed directly at seating/TV/desk; choose a high-corner angle  

4. Privacy-First Installation Best Practices  
 • Height & angle: Mount cameras at 8–12 feet, angled more downward than horizontal. This prevents detailed facial close-ups and makes cameras less obtrusive.  
 • No hidden cams: Transparency builds trust. Make cameras visible but unobtrusive (blend color, tidy cables).  
 • Signage & listing disclosure:  
   – Place a small “CCTV in operation” sign at main entrances.  
   – In your Airbnb listing description note “Security cameras monitor exterior doorways and common-area entry points only. No cameras in bedrooms/bathrooms.”  
   – Include a brief on-site house manual section (or QR-linked PDF) describing location and purpose.  
 • Access control: Only you (or a designated co-host) should have live-view or archiving rights. Log who accesses footage and purge old clips regularly (e.g. keep only 14–30 days).

5. Operational Protocols  
 • Emergency response: Use motion-alerts to your phone for large-scale events (door forced, glass break). Have a local contact or manager on call.  
 • Guest inquiries: Provide a single contact e-mail/phone for privacy questions. Offer to show camera views at check-in if they’re concerned.  
 • Data retention & deletion: Define a clear policy (“Footage deleted after 21 days unless flagged for incident review.”) Communicate that upfront.

6. Balancing Safety & Respect  
 • Opt out for sensitive stays: If a long-term guest or you host high-profile visitors, offer camera-free rental periods or temporary disabling.  
 • Human-first: Rely on devices to alert you, but treat every alert as a potential safety situation—not an intrusion. Always approach a triggered alarm with a welfare-check mindset.

7. Sample Disclosure Text for Your Listing  
“Security cameras record video only (≤1080p, no audio) at the:  
 • Exterior: front porch, back entry, driveway.  
 • Interior: main entrance hallway.  
No cameras in bedrooms or bathrooms. Video is motion-activated, stored securely for 21 days, and viewed only by hosts in case of safety or property incidents.”

By structuring your surveillance in this way you:  
 – Gain real deterrence and incident documentation  
 – Fully comply with Airbnb rules and privacy laws  
 – Provide clear transparency, boosting guest confidence rather than eroding it
